nodes.title: Primitive Greenberg μ-vanishing in BCS descent
nodes.statement: Let A=ℤ_p⟦Gal(K∞/K)⟧, B=ℤ_p⟦Gal(K∞⁻/K)⟧, A_R=R⟦Gal(K∞/K)⟧ and B_R=R⟦Gal(K∞⁻/K)⟧. Write π⁻:A_R→B_R for the cyclotomic-variable quotient. For the primitive BCS functions G_E=L_p^Gr(E/K) and B_E=L_p^BDP(E/K), one has (π⁻G_E)=(B_E), μ(B_E)=0 and μ(G_E)=0. Both functions are nonzero. The BCS B_E is the squared BCGS distribution, so (B_E)=(ℒ_E²) only after the existing normalization comparison is discharged. Consequently if J is an integral characteristic ideal in A_R and (G_E·G_EF)⊇J after inverting p, the same inclusion holds in A_R, provided the analogous hypotheses and primitive μ-vanishing hold for E^F. This clears denominators in the reverse product bound; it does not eliminate a p-primary defect in either individual Selmer ideal under residual irreducibility alone.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is an elliptic curve of conductor N; p>3 is a prime of good ordinary reduction.
K is imaginary quadratic with signed fundamental discriminant D_K<0 odd and not −3; every prime dividing N splits in K, and p=v v̄ splits in K with v fixed by the chosen p-adic embedding.
E[p] is irreducible over G_K. The same assumptions are required separately for the auxiliary quadratic twist E^F when it is used.

All functions and Selmer modules have the primitive BCS normalization, its ordinary Tate lattice and strict-at-v/unrestricted-at-v̄ Greenberg condition; completed unramified coefficients R=Ẑ_p^ur are retained.
proofSteps: BCS Proposition 4.2.2 imports Hsieh’s toric μ=0 theorem for the primitive anticyclotomic function. Use AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3h for that theorem, not the different Katz μ theorem needed at Eisenstein primes.

Use the analytic projection identity of CGS Proposition 2.4.5 (called 1.4.5 in the revision BCS cites). Its construction first proves integrality of the actual Greenberg function in Lemma 2.4.4, using the CM congruence-ideal divisibility from Hida–Tilouine Theorem 0.3 and Rubin’s theorem, plus the augmentation-factor exclusion from BDP22 Theorem A(i). L5a must import those independent inputs; a rational interpolation formula alone cannot replace them.
Reduction modulo p commutes with π⁻. Since π⁻G_E is nonzero modulo p, G_E is nonzero modulo p as well. This proves μ=0 without requiring the constant coefficient to be a unit.

At height-one primes away from (p), the rational inclusion gives the desired inequality. At (p), the generator G_E·G_EF has order zero whereas the integral ideal J has nonnegative order. Recover the integral inclusion using the supplier’s normal factorial characteristic-ideal calculus. No claim that μ(J)=0 is made.
acceptance: A series with zero constant coefficient and coefficient 1 in degree one has μ=0; the μ=0 test must not require a nonzero augmentation.
Replacing ℒ_E by ℒ_E² doubles every non-p height-one order. The comparison is of generated ideals, not equality of arbitrary period choices.
Multiplying the analytic generator by p destroys the denominator-clearing argument: for (p) and the unit ideal rational inclusion holds but integral inclusion fails.
No μ=0 assertion is exported for an arbitrary imprimitive Euler-factor modification.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.2.2 p.9; proof of Proposition 5.2.1 pp.9–10, especially (5.1)
sources.match: Primitive analytic μ-vanishing supplies exactly the p-height-one step in clearing denominators of the product reverse bound.
The actual integral two-variable Greenberg function projects to an associated anticyclotomic BDP function.

nodes.title: Anticyclotomic characteristic-ideal specialization
nodes.statement: With A,B,R,π⁻ as in primitive-greenberg-mu-vanishing, let X_E^(2) and X_E^− be the actual two-variable and anticyclotomic primitive Greenberg duals for T_pE. They use strict at v, unrestricted at v̄ and the fixed propagated away-p conditions. Assume X_E^− is B-torsion, as supplied independently by the Euler-system bound. When the integral imprimitive control and matching local Euler-factor comparisons below are supplied, X_E^(2) is A-torsion and char_B(X_E^−)B_R ⊆ π⁻(char_A(X_E^(2)))B_R. For E and E^F together this gives the corresponding inclusion of products. Combined with the normalized analytic projection and the integral two-variable Greenberg product bound, it yields (B_E B_EF) ⊇ char_B(X_E^−)char_B(X_EF^−)B_R. This is an inclusion for the specified arithmetic modules; characteristic ideals do not commute with arbitrary quotient maps.
hypotheses: E/ℚ is an elliptic curve of conductor N; p>3 is a prime of good ordinary reduction.
K is imaginary quadratic with signed fundamental discriminant D_K<0 odd and not −3; every prime dividing N splits in K, and p=v v̄ splits in K with v fixed by the chosen p-adic embedding.
E[p] is irreducible over G_K. The same assumptions are required separately for the auxiliary quadratic twist E^F when it is used.

All functions and Selmer modules have the primitive BCS normalization, its ordinary Tate lattice and strict-at-v/unrestricted-at-v̄ Greenberg condition; completed unramified coefficients R=Ẑ_p^ur are retained.

The imported Wan/Fujiwara and L5a product descent supply the integral two-variable Greenberg reverse bound, and both its analytic factors have the primitive μ-vanishing above. In particular their anticyclotomic images are nonzero.

For a finite Σ containing all ramified places away from p, supply the JSW restriction map X_Gr^Σ/(γ⁺−1)→X_ac^Σ with finite kernel and surjective target, and the precise finite-presentation/Fitting argument; an isomorphism is not assumed.

Supply exact primitive/imprimitive local module sequences on both towers, identifying their characteristic factors with the same nonzero Euler polynomials, compatible with π⁻ and the chosen Frobenius convention. Retain any correction factors until this comparison proves their cancellation.
Supply the needed extension of characteristic ideals from finite coefficient rings to the completed unramified coefficient ring; finite-flat base change alone does not state that extension.
proofSteps: Use the independent anticyclotomic Euler-system bound for torsionness, then SelmerIwasawaCohomology’s kernel-control with the actual strict/unrestricted local maps. JSW Lemma 3.4.1 gives finite errors in the imprimitive setting; it does not identify the primitive Selmer groups. Torsionness of the quotient by γ⁺−1, followed by Nakayama at that height-one prime, gives two-variable torsionness in this application.

Apply JSW Corollary 3.4.2 to obtain char_B(X_ac^Σ)⊆π⁻char_A(X_Gr^Σ). Its Fitting-ideal argument retains the finite kernel, and uses the principal reflexive closure rather than equating Fitting and characteristic ideals without a projective-dimension hypothesis.

Transport the local Euler factors through π⁻ using the exact local sequences, and cancel only their proved matching nonzero factors. The missing verification of this primitive step is explicitly recorded as a supplier gap.

Extend the resulting primitive inclusion to B_R, multiply the statements for E and E^F and combine with the analytic projection and two-variable reverse bound. Nonzero projected analytic functions rule out the zero-ideal/torsion ambiguity in this application.
acceptance: The comparison has direction char(X_ac)⊆π⁻char(X_Gr); the reverse inclusion is not supplied by JSW.
A finite kernel contributes no height-one divisor over B, but can change the initial Fitting ideal. The proof must keep those assertions distinct.
The printed JSW corollary requires an imprimitive Σ. An application with Σ empty must show the local-factor comparison explicitly.

There is no analytic-rank-one hypothesis in the BCS endpoint. Any use of JSW’s other standing assumptions must be justified from the local proof or left as this recorded control gap, not silently added to the endpoint.
The torsion Greenberg dual here is distinct from the rank-one all-p ordinary dual used by the CS determinant comparison.

sources: bcs-v2 Lemma 5.2.3 and its residual-restriction argument, p.10
auxiliaryFieldVerification.detail: First derive (irr_K) from (irr_Q): if the restriction to G_K were reducible, the irreducible two-dimensional representation would be induced from K. Inertia at any prime dividing D_K would then permute its two lines nontrivially, contradicting unramifiedness away from Np and gcd(D_K,Np)=1. For the theorem’s fixed K, choose a prime q≡1 mod 8|D_K| with prescribed nonzero square/nonsquare residue classes modulo each odd ℓ|Np: (q/p)=−1 and (q/ℓ)=−1 exactly when ℓ|N and ℓ≡−1 mod p. The moduli are coprime because (Heeg),(spl) imply gcd(D_K,Np)=1. Dirichlet/Chebotarev gives infinitely many such q. Then F=ℚ(√q) has D_F=q, q splits in K, and conditions (i)–(iii) hold, including splitting at 2 when 2|N. Avoid the finitely many F contained in the compositum of K and the residual splitting field; restriction to G_FK then preserves the G_K image, giving (iv). Exclude the p=5 exceptional field. The final residual-restriction argument in Lemma 5.2.3 gives (v) under these exclusions, and (vi) is explicit. Thus the local/avoidance construction can be performed without changing K. This expands the existing target proof; it creates no second auxiliary-field node. The quadratic twist remains ordinary at p and has new conductor primes only among those dividing D_F, which split in K; its residual restriction stays irreducible. For the surjective branch, twisting preserves the commutator image SL₂(F_p) and the surjective cyclotomic determinant, hence the full GL₂(F_p) image.
